c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.

g.passage: Ecologists long assumed that the bright orange coloring of the poison frog Oophaga granulifera served only to warn predators of the toxins in its skin. Field observations in Costa Rica by biologist Lena Marquart complicate that view. She found that frogs in populations with the most vivid coloring were not consistently more toxic than duller frogs; ______ the brightest males attracted noticeably more females during the breeding season, suggesting that coloration may also function as a sexual signal.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 세미콜론 앞 문장은 밝은 색이 독성(경고 기능)과 일관되게 연결되지 않는다는 것, 즉 기존 설명을 뒷받침하지 못하는 결과다. 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 밝은 색이 짝짓기에서는 분명한 이점을 보였다는 대조적 결과이므로 대조의 A가 적절하다. B는 독성과 무관하다는 사실이 암컷 유인의 원인이 되지 않으므로 인과가 성립하지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 사례가 아니라 다른 기능을 보여 주므로 틀리다. D는 두 결과가 같은 방향의 발견처럼 보일 수 있으나, 하나는 연관이 없다는 결과이고 다른 하나는 뚜렷한 연관을 보여 주어 서로 대조된다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the semicolon shows that bright coloring was not consistently linked to toxicity, a result that fails to support the warning-signal idea. The next part shows that bright coloring did have a clear payoff in attracting mates, which contrasts with that first result, so A is correct. B is wrong because the frogs' color not matching their toxicity doesn't cause females to prefer brighter males. C is wrong because the mating result isn't an example of the toxicity finding; it points to a different function. D might seem to fit because both are new findings, but one shows no consistent link and the other shows a clear link, so they contrast instead of being alike.
g.design: Both clauses are field findings that challenge the old assumption, so "therefore" and "similarly" seem partly plausible at first. Only a careful reading shows the contrast between "no consistent link" and "a clear link."

- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.

g.passage: In her 2019 novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, Welsh author Carys Penhallow imitates the leisurely, digressive narration of Victorian fiction: chapters open with long descriptions of weather and furniture, and the narrator frequently pauses to address the reader directly. Several reviewers assumed that Penhallow was simply paying affectionate tribute to writers such as George Eliot. The novel's final chapter, ______ reveals that the chatty narrator has been hiding the heroine's fate all along, turning the familiar Victorian voice into a tool of deliberate deception.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 평론가들이 이 소설을 빅토리아 시대 작가에 대한 단순한 오마주로 보았다고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 마지막 장이 그 익숙한 서술 목소리를 의도적인 기만의 도구로 바꾼다고 밝힌다. 이는 평론가들의 가정을 뒤집는 내용이므로 대조를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 마지막 장이 빅토리아식 서술 모방의 한 예로 보일 수 있어 그럴듯하지만, 뒤 문장은 단순한 모방을 넘어 그 가정을 반박하므로 예시가 아니다. C는 마지막 장의 반전이 평론가들의 가정에서 비롯된 결과가 아니므로 틀렸다. D는 두 문장이 같은 방향의 내용을 이어 간다고 보지만, 실제로는 서로 반대되는 해석을 제시하므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says reviewers thought the novel was simply an affectionate tribute to Victorian writers. The sentence with the blank then shows that the final chapter turns that familiar voice into a tool of deliberate deception. This overturns the reviewers' assumption, so the contrast transition in B is correct. A may look tempting because the final chapter still uses Victorian-style narration, but the sentence challenges the "simple tribute" reading instead of giving an example of it. C is wrong because the twist is not a result of what the reviewers assumed, and D is wrong because the two sentences point in opposite directions rather than making similar points.
g.design: There is no word like "but" to signal the shift. Students have to see that "simply paying tribute" is set up as an assumption and that the deception reveal pushes back against it. A and D are tempting because the final chapter still uses the Victorian style, and C sounds plausible if the text is skimmed as a cause-and-effect chain.

g.passage: Along the coast of Bangladesh, engineers once relied on earthen embankments called polders to keep tidal water off farmland. The walls worked as intended, but they also blocked the sediment that tides had always spread across the floodplain. Over several decades, the land inside many polders sank while riverbeds outside them rose with trapped silt. ______ some enclosed fields now sit lower than the channels beside them, leaving them waterlogged after heavy rains and harder to drain than before the embankments were built.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 제방 안쪽 땅은 가라앉고 바깥 하천 바닥은 높아졌다는 원인을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 때문에 일부 농지가 수로보다 낮아져 배수가 어려워졌다는 결과를 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 제방이 의도대로 작동했다는 앞부분과 대조되는 것처럼 보이지만, 바로 앞 문장과 이어지는 내용은 반전이 아니라 그 논리적 귀결이다. B는 뒤 문장이 구체적 사례처럼 보여 끌리지만, 앞 문장의 사례가 아니라 그로 인해 생긴 새로운 결과다. D는 두 문장 모두 문제점을 다룬다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 별개의 유사한 현상을 나열하는 관계가 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: land inside the polders sank while the riverbeds outside rose. The sentence after it gives the effect: some fields now sit lower than the nearby channels and are hard to drain. That makes C the best answer. A may seem possible because the passage first says the walls worked as intended, but the final sentence follows logically from the sentence right before it rather than reversing it. B is tempting because the final sentence sounds specific, but it describes a new result, not an example of the sinking and rising. D fails because the final sentence does not add a separate, similar problem. It describes what happened because of the problem already mentioned.
g.design: There is no word in the passage that directly signals cause and effect, so students must see that the relative heights described in the earlier sentences explain the waterlogging. The "worked as intended" clause makes A appealing, and the specific detail in the last sentence makes B appealing.

g.passage: When the Erie Canal opened in 1825, many merchants in Philadelphia assumed their city's long-standing trade networks would shield it from competition with New York. Historian Elena Marsh argues that this confidence was misplaced. Because the canal cut the cost of shipping grain from the Great Lakes region by roughly 90 percent, western farmers began routing their harvests eastward through Albany and down the Hudson River rather than overland toward Pennsylvania. ______ by the 1840s, New York had handled a far larger share of the nation's exports than Philadelphia, a gap that Pennsylvania's own expensive canal system never managed to close.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 운하로 운송비가 급감하자 서부 농민들이 곡물을 뉴욕 쪽으로 보내기 시작했다는 원인을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 1840년대 뉴욕이 수출 비중에서 필라델피아를 크게 앞섰다는 결과를 제시하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 필라델피아 상인들의 자신감과 대조되는 듯 보이지만, 바로 앞 문장과 뒤 문장은 대립이 아니라 인과로 이어지므로 틀리다. B는 뒤 문장이 앞 내용의 구체적 사례처럼 보일 수 있으나, 수출 비중 격차는 농민들의 운송 경로 변화의 한 예가 아니라 그 결과이다. C는 두 문장이 모두 뉴욕에 유리한 변화를 말해 비슷해 보이지만, 별개의 유사한 사례를 나열하는 관계가 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a cause: the canal slashed shipping costs, so western farmers began sending grain through New York. The sentence after the blank gives the outcome: by the 1840s New York handled far more of the nation's exports than Philadelphia. That cause-to-effect link makes D correct. A might seem to fit because the passage contrasts with the Philadelphia merchants' confidence, but the two sentences around the blank don't conflict; one follows from the other. B treats the export gap as an example of farmers changing their routes, when it's actually a consequence of that change. C would introduce a separate, parallel development, but the second sentence results directly from the first.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤가 인과 관계지만 어휘 단서가 없다. 지문 앞부분의 '자신감이 틀렸다'는 내용은 대조(A)로 유도하고, 구체적 수치는 예시(B)로 유도하도록 설계했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 목표(비교·대조·특징 강조 등)에 맞게 서로 다른 메모를 골라 결합해야 하는 문제. 오답은 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 목표에서 벗어난다.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the nineteenth century, many European cities lacked public clocks that agreed with one another; each town kept its own local "sun time."
- In 1847, most British railway companies adopted Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), often called "railway time," to coordinate train schedules.
- Bristol, about 190 kilometers west of London, kept its local time roughly ten minutes behind GMT for several years after the railways switched.
- The Corn Exchange in Bristol installed a clock with two minute hands, one showing local time and one showing railway time.
- By 1855, the vast majority of public clocks in Britain displayed GMT.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize that the shift to a standardized time in Britain was not immediate everywhere. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although most British railway companies adopted GMT in 1847, Bristol continued to keep local time for several years, even displaying both times on its Corn Exchange clock.
In 1847, most British railway companies adopted Greenwich Mean Time, and by 1855 the vast majority of public clocks in Britain displayed it.
Before railway time, many European cities kept their own local "sun time," so their public clocks often failed to agree with one another.
Bristol, about 190 kilometers west of London, had a local time that ran roughly ten minutes behind Greenwich Mean Time.
g.explanation: 목표는 표준시 전환이 모든 곳에서 즉시 일어나지 않았음을 강조하는 것이다. A는 1847년 철도의 GMT 채택과 브리스톨이 수년간 지역 시간을 유지하며 두 시간을 함께 표시한 사실을 대조해 전환의 지연을 분명히 보여 준다. B는 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 전환이 순조롭게 퍼졌다는 인상을 주어 지연을 강조하지 못한다. C는 표준화 이전 상황만 설명할 뿐 전환 과정을 다루지 않는다. D는 브리스톨과 GMT의 시차만 말하고, 철도가 바꾼 뒤에도 브리스톨이 지역 시간을 유지했다는 점은 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: The goal is to emphasize that the shift to standardized time didn't happen immediately everywhere. A sets the railways' 1847 adoption of GMT against Bristol keeping its local time for years afterward, even showing both times on one clock, so it clearly highlights the delay. B uses accurate notes, but it makes the shift sound smooth and widespread instead of emphasizing any delay. C describes only the situation before standardization and says nothing about how the shift happened. D gives only the time difference between Bristol and GMT and leaves out the key fact that Bristol held on to local time after the railways had switched.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 두 메모를 연결해야 한다. 철도가 GMT를 채택한 연도와 브리스톨이 그 뒤에도 지역 시간을 유지했다는 사실이다. 오답 B와 D는 관련 있는 정확한 메모를 쓰지만, 목표 중 '즉시 전환되지 않았다'는 부분을 놓친다.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Traditional concrete production releases large amounts of carbon dioxide, mainly from heating limestone to make cement.
- In 2021, engineers in Norway tested a concrete mix in which crushed seashells replaced 40 percent of the limestone.
- The seashell mix reached 92 percent of the strength of standard concrete after 28 days.
- The seashell mix produced about 30 percent less carbon dioxide during manufacturing.
- Seashells are a waste product of the seafood industry and are often sent to landfills.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize a trade-off of the seashell concrete mix. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Because seashells are a seafood industry waste product often sent to landfills, using them in concrete could reduce the carbon dioxide released when limestone is heated.
The seashell concrete mix cut manufacturing carbon dioxide emissions by about 30 percent, though it reached only 92 percent of the strength of standard concrete after 28 days.
In 2021, engineers in Norway tested a concrete mix in which crushed seashells replaced 40 percent of the limestone normally used to make cement.
The seashell concrete mix not only produced about 30 percent less carbon dioxide but also made use of seashells that would otherwise end up in landfills.
g.explanation: 목표는 '트레이드오프', 즉 얻는 이점과 잃는 대가를 함께 보여 주는 것이다. B는 탄소 배출 30% 감소(이점)와 강도가 표준의 92%에 그친다는 점(대가)을 'though'로 연결해 목표를 정확히 달성한다. D는 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 두 가지 이점만 나열하므로 대가가 빠져 있다. A는 폐기물 활용과 탄소 감소 가능성을 연결할 뿐 단점이 없다. C는 실험 내용만 소개하는 배경 설명이다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to show a trade-off, meaning a benefit along with a cost. B does this: it pairs the 30 percent drop in carbon dioxide (the benefit) with strength reaching only 92 percent of standard concrete (the cost), joined by "though." D uses accurate notes, but it lists two benefits and leaves out any cost. A links waste reuse to lower emissions, but it never mentions a downside. C only describes the experiment as background information.
g.design: 오답 D는 두 메모를 결합한 '장점+장점' 구조라 훑어 읽으면 대조처럼 보이고, A도 두 메모를 결합해 비교가 필요하도록 설계했다.
